rows.proposed_prompt:
You are an expert in Sanskrit grammar (vyakarana).

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): जभँ॒   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): गात्रविनामे

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lat (present)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Prathama (third person)
- vacana (number): Eka (singular)
rows.source_limits: The nonnasal jabh form is an attributed printed Kshira reading; the nasal form has a positive num derivation. This is not an optional-num claim.
